answer: An agent economy scheduling timber haulers, vineyard trellis monitors, and comet observatory sensors resists Sybil attacks using transitive credit networks. Participants route consensus votes through bilateral trust lines formed by historical trade. An attacker incurs the verifiable, scarce cost of tying up capital and building real settlement history per identity. However, this creates liquidity bottlenecks around central nodes and marginalizes new, unlinked agents.
